pattern.top_pattern: NY EPO acute hospital spend shows both pricing and low-volume inpatient pressure
pattern.what_is_impacting: NY EPO acute hospital inpatient spend
key_driver_codes: Intracranial Hemorrhage or Cerebral Infarction with MCC
Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures without CC/MCC
pattern.pattern_details: NY EPO acute hospital costs rose across a small set of inpatient episodes, with both additional cases and higher paid amounts per admission contributing. Bowel surgery and bronchitis/asthma added low-volume mixed pressure, while stroke-related admissions were purely price-led. This looks like a small but concentrated hospital pricing and utilization pocket.
pattern.why_it_matters: Even a small EPO inpatient block can generate avoidable trend if price variance is not separated from true case growth.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Audit NY EPO inpatient payment variance for these DRGs and confirm whether contract terms, outlier reimbursement, or isolated case mix drove the per-admission increase.
pattern.validation_reason: The pattern is low-volume and concentrated, so pricing and case classification should be confirmed before broader reimbursement action.
evidence_summary: NY EPO acute hospital spend increased about $159K.
Bowel surgery and bronchitis/asthma cases added about $90K across 2 claims.
Stroke-related admissions added about $69K with no claim growth, making part of the increase unit-cost-led.
All components are concentrated in a small inpatient book.
